props.covers: Spacing is semantic and local: one exact gap repeats within a peer group, a wider exact gutter repeats between sections, the ladder names each rung from section padding up through the section gutter, and the crowding lint marks the minimum arrow corridor rather than a target spacing amount.

text.insert: Choose a gap wide enough for the group's content, wires, and labels, then repeat it exactly. The repetition is the signal that the members are peers.

Section padding — 48px of air between a section border and the nearest child, on every side. It is the shortest rung: a frame sits closer to its own children than any two peers sit to each other, which is what makes the frame read as theirs.

Sibling gaps — 144px between side-by-side peers, 72px between stacked peers. Against a 288×96 node that is half a node width across and three quarters of a node height down, so a row repeats on a 432px pitch and a column on a 168px pitch.

Section-to-section gutters — 144px across, 160px down. The horizontal gutter matches the sibling gap because separate columns already read as separate; the vertical gutter is more than twice the stacked sibling gap, and that jump is what tells a reader where one section ends and the next begins.

What the ladder adds up to — a board whose node area is about 15% of its board area. Air is the majority of a finished board; hold the rungs, keep two or three nodes in a section, and that ratio arrives on its own. A board reading well above it was built by tightening the rungs.
Uniformity carries meaning: same size plus the same gap says that nodes are peers. A near-match reads as an accidental exception.
Content comes first: size each box for its label with comfortable padding, then make peers match the largest member before setting the repeated pitch.
Copy instead of estimating: use a peer's exact digest size and pitch so the next member lands on the same register and gap.
Every label and routed wire owns clear air. Within a section, centers stay on one line; between sections, use one wider gutter and repeat that gutter too.

The crowding warning marks the corridor floor for sibling nodes: under 80px side by side or under 48px stacked. These thresholds protect route clearance; they are not preferred spacing values — the rungs above are.
